task.start: Pointed at this file, in any session, you build from the files alone: on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin, read them whole before you write anything, and take nothing said earlier in the session, or remembered from other work, as authority. Read whole, in this order: specs/root.xml; specs/rules.xml; specs/lessons.xml; this file; then every file under reads. Cut the branch SF-156-engine-mysql-v2-<model>-<effort> from the head of main. Every commit message starts with SF-156 and carries no attribution of any kind. Build the steps in their order; after each, run its gate and show the output, its exit code read on its own, never through a pipe, before anything is committed (lesson exit-code-hidden). Push the branch and open the PR into main titled "SF-156 Objective 5 of 11: the Engine trait and engine_mysql in Rust v2", its body as root method pr gives it: the gate table with each gate's output, then the hand-off notes. Before every step, say in one line what it is and how long it takes; after it, its result. What these files do not say is a stop: ask, never guess.
task.piece: The app imports a live MySQL server into a design and writes a design back as SQL, through an Engine trait that core, the server and the canvas use without ever naming MySQL. engine_mysql is a plugin like any other: its Rust crate beside its schema in engines/mysql. It is designed from MySQL's catalog and the plugin's tables, in idiomatic Rust, correct first and its speed checked (decision correctness-first), and proven by round trips on seven live servers, server against server (decision proof-server-against-server): what it reads lands and is written back exactly as the server holds it (decision exact-migration). engines/mysql/*.py is the prototype: read for facts, never changed, never called, never ported.

never.rule: Never port, mirror or reproduce the Python prototype. Read it only to learn which catalog table or statement gives which fact. Forbidden in the Rust: string keys joined with a separator (as "db|kind|name"); a pair as a two-element list or vector; a fake database or namespace name for the server's own objects (as "@server"); the text None or Python's JSON format in any output; a value that crosses the Engine trait as untyped JSON. The gate no-python-shape fails the build on each.

Nothing is written from memory or a guess: a crate's version from crates.io, a licence from tools/app/licences.py, a column's name and type from engines/mysql/schema and schema/cortex, a catalog table's columns from the MySQL server itself. Cite the source in the commit message.
If a step's design turns out wrong, stop, say so, and design it again from this file; never patch a wrong design.
Build what this file says and nothing more. Work found on the way is reported in the PR, never started.
Before every step and every wait (a build, a test, CI), one line: what it is, how long it takes; after it, its result with the output that proves it.

Every format the code reads is first seen on a live server of each version it applies to (tools/mysql/show.py), and every test of a parser reads that server's text, pasted as it came, with the server and the date in a comment beside it; never text written from memory (lesson catalog-is-not-sql: the first build's partition parser passed on backticks no server writes).

Nothing the server holds is dropped, reduced or defaulted on the way in or out (decision exact-migration). A fact this file maps and no sample exercises is listed in the PR as unproven; a fact the server shows that this file does not map is a stop.

mapping.note: Every column the import writes, and where its value comes from. I_S is information_schema. "SHOW" is the object's SHOW CREATE statement, read for the clause named. A source marked verify is to be confirmed on the live servers (tools/mysql/show.py --server S "statement") before it is used; if it is not there, the column is left as unfilled lists it, and the PR says so. A column not in this mapping or in unfilled is a stop. Empty strings the server gives for "none" (a comment of '') are stored as NULL. Every id is a UUIDv7 made at the import (step 6).

quirks.note: Facts the servers were found to have (objective 3, docs/live-mysql.xml): each is handled where named.
quirks.quirk: 8.0's COLUMNS.GENERATION_EXPRESSION escapes the quotes of the expression; the expression is taken from SHOW CREATE TABLE's column line, between GENERATED ALWAYS AS ( and its matching ), quotes and backslashes respected.
STATISTICS.SUB_PART gives a SPATIAL index's part an internal prefix of 32 the statement never writes: not stored.

A view's definition read from outside its database has every name qualified by the database; the qualifier of its own database is removed outside strings, so it is the definition written from inside it.

ROUTINES.ROUTINE_DEFINITION is NULL without the routine privileges, and the parameter list and return type are normalised by PARAMETERS: the parameter list, return type and body come from SHOW CREATE as written.
EXECUTE_AT, STARTS, ENDS and INTERVAL_VALUE are read cast to CHAR, so their text is the server's.
A rule not written reads back as RESTRICT on 5.7 and NO ACTION on 8.0 and later; it is stored as read, and the writer never writes NO ACTION.
The server's own accounts (root, mysql.%, Percona's percona.telemetry) and Percona's telemetry component are the server's, never a design's.
A MERGE table's UNION names its tables without their database: it is created after USE of its database.
A component may hold accounts to rules (validate_password) that an account made without a password breaks: components are installed after the accounts.
A JavaScript body is quoted with $$: programs are written under DELIMITER $sf_end$.
Everything on the wire is utf8mb4; the server converts each value from its own character set.

8.0's catalog escapes the quotes of a CHECK_CLAUSE and of an expression default's COLUMN_DEFAULT (live, 8.0.46, 2026-11-28: CHECK (s IN ('a','b')) reads back (`s` in (_utf8mb4\'a\',_utf8mb4\'b\'))); both are taken from SHOW CREATE TABLE as written, as a generated column's expression is (quirk generated-escaped).

8.0's COLUMN_DEFAULT gives a BINARY or VARBINARY column's literal default as the hex of its bytes (live: DEFAULT 'ab' reads back 0x6162): stored as given and written back as the hex literal, unquoted.

SHOW CREATE TABLE writes an ordinary partition or subpartition name bare, without backticks, and gives every listed partition and subpartition its ENGINE (live, 8.0.46: (PARTITION p0 VALUES LESS THAN (10) (SUBPARTITION s0 ENGINE = InnoDB, ...)); a name is read bare or quoted, and SUBPARTITION BY and SUBPARTITIONS n are never taken for a subpartition.

information_schema.PARTITIONS has one row per subpartition of a subpartitioned table, and its PARTITION_COMMENT is that subpartition's own when the subpartitions are listed one by one (live: p_old/s_old_b gives s_old_b's comment), and the partition's, repeated on every row, when they are counted (SUBPARTITIONS n): listed, each subpartition keeps its comment and the partition has none; counted, the partition keeps it.

5.7 prints a grant's column list in its own hash order, which no order of writing reproduces (live, 2026-11-28: SELECT (name, email), UPDATE (name) prints SELECT (email, name); SELECT (email, name), UPDATE (name) prints SELECT (name, email)): column privileges are read in the server's order, and the round trip compares a grant's column list as a set.

A caching_sha2_password hash is binary: SHOW CREATE USER writes it as raw bytes unless the session sets print_identified_with_as_hex (8.0.17 and later), when it is a 0x hex literal; 5.7's hashes are text. The read's session sets it through a versioned comment older servers skip (SET @x = 1 /*!80017 , SESSION print_identified_with_as_hex = ON */).

mysql_async's pool resets a connection each time it is returned (reset_connection, on by default), which clears the session: the read's session settings are set with OptsBuilder::setup, run on every new connection and after every reset, never with init, run once (mysql_async 0.37.1, src/opts/mod.rs; lesson driver-resets-the-session).

5.7 has no CHECK constraints, invisible columns or indexes, expression or descending parts, spatial reference systems of its own, DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION, SCHEMATA_EXTENSIONS, roles (role_edges, default_roles), dynamic privileges or components: none is asked of it.

task.equal: Two designs are equal when, for every table of the mapping, their rows are the same set once each row's id and design are dropped and every column holding an id is replaced by the name path of the row it points to: a namespace by its name under its parent's; an object by its namespace's path, kind and name; a column by its object's path and its name; an index or constraint by its object's path and its name; an index part or constraint column by its owner's path and position; a partition by its table's path, its parent partition's name and its name; a dependency by its object's and its target's paths, as and position. Every other column is compared exactly, positions among them. Between server A and server B (one image, fresh) nothing is expected to differ. tools/app/mysql.py reads both designs as cortex_reader and lists each difference by table and path. The designs being equal is not enough (lesson design-against-design): the servers are compared too (decision proof-server-against-server). Every object's DDL as the server writes it, SHOW CREATE TABLE, VIEW, PROCEDURE, FUNCTION, TRIGGER, EVENT and LIBRARY of every object of design A, SHOW CREATE DATABASE of every database, and SHOW CREATE USER with every line of SHOW GRANTS of every account and role, must be identical on A and B, but where the server itself writes a fact in an order of its own: on 5.7 a trigger's header is compared with its typing undone (5.7 keeps a trigger's CREATE as typed; its body byte for byte), and a grant's column list is compared as a set (quirk grant-column-order).

module.step: Add crates/engine and engines/mysql to the workspace members and the crates above to workspace.dependencies. Remove clippy's pedantic group and its two allows from workspace.lints: clippy's own lints with warnings failing the build stay (lesson style-lints-cost-hours). deny.toml allows exactly the seven licences above.

step.name: the store, from the review of #163

module.step: Endpoint gains statement_timeout: Duration (default one minute), sent to the server on every connection as the option -c statement_timeout; every connection sets TCP keepalives: idle 30 s, interval 10 s, 3 retries. Store::read rolls its transaction back when its work fails, before the connection goes back to its pool.

module.public: Engine, Registry, Source, ImportReport, Mapped, Fidelity, EngineError

step.name: what MySQL holds, as MySQL lists it

module.step: One typed struct per catalog source, its fields the source's columns by their MySQL names in snake case, read with mysql_async as typed rows (never as JSON): information_schema SCHEMATA, SCHEMATA_EXTENSIONS (8.0.22 and later), TABLES (base tables), COLUMNS, STATISTICS, KEY_COLUMN_USAGE joined to REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS, CHECK_CONSTRAINTS joined to TABLE_CONSTRAINTS (8.0.16 and later), PARTITIONS, VIEWS, VIEW_TABLE_USAGE (8.0.13 and later), ROUTINES, PARAMETERS, TRIGGERS, EVENTS, LIBRARIES and ROUTINE_LIBRARIES (where the server has them), INNODB_TABLESPACES (8.0) or INNODB_SYS_TABLESPACES (5.7) with FILES, ST_SPATIAL_REFERENCE_SYSTEMS (8.0, user systems only), RESOURCE_GROUPS (8.0, not the two defaults), COMPRESSION_DICTIONARY or XTRADB_ZIP_DICT (Percona), USER_PRIVILEGES, SCHEMA_PRIVILEGES, TABLE_PRIVILEGES, COLUMN_PRIVILEGES; mysql.user (never root, mysql.%, percona.%), mysql.role_edges and mysql.default_roles (8.0), mysql.procs_priv, mysql.proxies_priv, mysql.servers, mysql.func, mysql.component (8.0, never Percona's telemetry). Each struct holds exactly what the mapping takes from its source. Every source is asked with the system databases excluded (mysql, information_schema, performance_schema, sys). Which sources a version has is decided once, from the version and a probe of information_schema.COLUMNS, never by trying and failing.

The version first (SELECT VERSION(), @@version_comment, @@character_set_server, @@collation_server, @@lower_case_table_names, @@sql_mode). The design's version is the server's major.minor (8.0.46 is 8.0); a version not in cortex.engine_versions for mysql is refused before anything else is read, the error naming the server's version and the declared ones. The flavor is percona when @@version_comment holds "Percona", mysql otherwise; a managed service's flavor (rds, aurora, cloudsql) cannot be told from the server and is only ever given by the caller. A pool of Source.connections connections, each session set on every new connection and again after every reset (quirk driver-session-reset) with SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY, SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 5, SET SESSION max_execution_time = 10000, SET SESSION sql_mode = '', SET NAMES utf8mb4, and the hex hashes of quirk hex-hashes; never USE, every statement names its database. The catalog sources of step 4 are asked at once, each one query, concurrently over the pool. SHOW CREATE TABLE, VIEW, PROCEDURE, FUNCTION and USER, and SHOW GRANTS, are asked only for what the catalog does not give (a table's AUTO_INCREMENT, TABLESPACE, UNION and INSERT_METHOD; an index's clauses; a generated column's expression, a check's expression and an expression default as written, which 8.0's catalog escapes; each listed partition's and subpartition's own options; a view's ALGORITHM and definition, every `<its database>`. qualifier outside a string removed, since read from outside its database the server qualifies every name; a routine's parameter list and body as written; an account's settings and its password's hash, never a password, which no server gives), Source.connections at a time over the pool, in any order, their results placed by key. Everything on the wire is utf8mb4. The read returns a Catalog: every struct of step 4 in vectors, plus the SHOW results by object.

step.name: from the catalog to the store's rows

module.step: Every column is filled as the mapping says, from the source it names, and the columns of unfilled as it says; nothing else. Each object is given its UUIDv7 once (Uuid::now_v7), in a map keyed by a typed key: ObjectKey { scope: Scope, kind: Kind, name: String } where Scope is Database(String) or Server, Kind an enum of engine_mysql's 16 kinds (engines/mysql/seeds/engine.sql). Every reference (a column's table, an index's columns, a key's referenced table and columns, a view's uses, a routine's libraries, a privilege's object, a grant's role) is resolved through that map to an id; a reference to nothing in the catalog is left out for a view's uses and is an error anywhere else. The rows are built column-wise: for each destination table, one struct of vectors, one vector per column, in the table's column order. The server is namespace "server" (position 1), each database a namespace under it; the server's own objects (accounts, roles, tablespaces, servers, loadable functions, components, resource groups, spatial reference systems, compression dictionaries) are objects of the server's namespace. engines/mysql's public API is Mysql alone: every other module is the crate's own, not pub, so the compiler reports dead code (the first build exposed ten modules and hid six dead items).

step.name: stored in one operation, one statement per table

module.step: Inside Store::write as the plugin's account, begin_operation(design, turn, "import", "imported <version> from <host>") first, then for each destination table, parents before children (namespaces, objects, columns, indexes, index_parts, constraints, constraint_columns, dependencies, then engine_mysql's tables), one statement: INSERT INTO t (c1, …, cn) SELECT u.c1, …, u.cn FROM unnest($1::type1[], …, $n::typen[]) AS u(c1, …, cn). A column bound as another type than its own is cast in the select list: a NUMERIC position bound as int4[]; a JSONB column (engine_mysql.accounts.attributes) bound as text[], its value the JSON text the server gave, and cast u.attributes::jsonb; no value crosses as serde_json::Value. A table with no rows is skipped. An import is at most one statement per destination table plus begin_operation's two, however many objects; ImportReport.statements counts them. The closure builds nothing: it binds vectors built before it, so a retry re-runs only the inserts. Before anything is sent, a table whose columns differ in length is an error naming the table and the column (unnest pads a shorter array with NULLs, so an unevenly built table would be stored wrong without a word); a refusal of the store names the table it was storing, its SQLSTATE kept so a collision is still retried.

step.name: from the store's rows to a design

module.step: As the plugin's account, one query per table of the design's rows, read as typed rows; assembled into a Design: maps by id (namespaces, objects, columns by object in position order, indexes with their parts, constraints with their columns, dependencies, and each object's engine_mysql row). No string key is built.

The SQL a MySQL server of the design's version loads, in this order, which follows what the server checks when each statement runs (lesson order-by-real-dependencies): SET NAMES utf8mb4, SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS = 0, SET UNIQUE_CHECKS = 0, SET sql_mode = 'NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION'; CREATE DATABASE each (its character set, collation, encryption); the server's objects tables need (tablespaces, spatial reference systems, compression dictionaries, servers, loadable functions, resource groups); CREATE TABLE each, a MERGE table after the tables it unites (columns, indexes, foreign and check keys, options, partitioning), each preceded by USE of its database, since a MERGE table's UNION names its tables without their database; SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS = 1; then, under DELIMITER $sf_end$, libraries, procedures and functions, each preceded by USE of its database and its session (sql_mode, character_set_client, collation_connection), and DELIMITER ; with SET NAMES utf8mb4 and the script's sql_mode again; views in dependency order (a topological sort; a cycle is an error naming the views), after the routines because CREATE VIEW checks that every function it calls exists while a routine's body is not checked until it runs, each with its client character set, and SET NAMES utf8mb4 after them; then, under DELIMITER $sf_end$ again, triggers (ordered by table, timing, event and action order, each FOLLOWS the one before it in its group) and events, each preceded by USE of its database and its session (and an event's time_zone), closed as the routines are; accounts and roles, each account with its hash (CREATE USER … IDENTIFIED WITH 'plugin' AS hash, a 0x hex hash unquoted: decision exact-migration; never an account without its hash where the design holds one), role grants, privileges grouped by grantee, target and grant option, default roles; INSTALL COMPONENT; then ALTER DATABASE … READ ONLY = 1 where so, last, since a read-only database refuses every CREATE in it; SET UNIQUE_CHECKS = 1. A string literal written inside a program's own session (a routine's or event's comment, an event's time zone) is written as that session's sql_mode reads it: under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES only its quotes are doubled. A column's literal default is quoted, but a BIT column's b'…' and a binary column's 0x… hex (quirk binary-default-hex), written as they are. A foreign key's rule is written for every rule but NO ACTION (quirk fk-rules). A value a statement needs and the design lacks is an error naming the object, never written as a placeholder.

Every MySQL column type to an Arrow DataType with its fidelity: the integer types exact, unsigned to Arrow's unsigned; DECIMAL(p,s) to Decimal128(p,s) (Decimal256 above 38); FLOAT, DOUBLE exact; CHAR, VARCHAR, TEXT types to Utf8 (approximate: the length is not kept); BINARY, VARBINARY, BLOB types to Binary (approximate); DATE to Date32; DATETIME and TIMESTAMP to Timestamp (microseconds; TIMESTAMP with UTC); TIME to Time64; YEAR to Int16 (approximate); JSON to Utf8 (approximate: JSON kept as text); ENUM and SET to Utf8 (approximate: the allowed values not kept); BIT(n) to UInt64 (approximate); spatial types to Binary (lost: the geometry's type and SRID).
pub struct Mysql; impl Engine for Mysql: id "mysql", namespace "engine_mysql", import (step 5 then steps 6 and 7), write (step 8 then step 9), arrow_type (step 10).

The binary's registry holds Mysql. schema-forge import --engine mysql --source mysql://user@host:port --design NAME [--flavor F] [--tls] [--connections N, default 4] [--password-env VAR] [--host, --port, --accounts-file as check]: reads the server's version first (step 5), creates the design with that version and the flavor read or given, opens an import turn as the app, imports, commits, and prints the ImportReport. When the import fails, the turn, which holds no operation, is rejected, so the design is never left held; the error is printed and the exit code is 1. When the import succeeds and its commit fails (a lost connection), the turn holds the import's operation and cannot be rejected: the commit is tried again, twice, after a short pause, and if it still fails the design this command made is deleted, so it is never left held either; the error names the design and the turn when even that fails. schema-forge write --design NAME [the store's options]: prints the design's SQL. A MySQL password comes only from the environment variable named, never from an argument.

python3 tools/app/mysql.py --server mysql:5.7|mysql:8.0|mysql:8.4|mysql:9.7|percona:5.7|percona:8.0|percona:8.4 [--private FILE] [--option OPTION ...] [--source mysql://user@host:port [--password-file FILE]]; percona:<version> is Docker Hub's percona/percona-server:<version>. A store in a container (tools/sf/store.py, published); server A, a container that also publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 (a subclass of tools/sf/servers.py's MySQL defined in tools/app/mysql.py), with the samples of tools/mysql/samples loaded in this order (common.sql, the version's own files, found.sql, server.sql, server-8.0.sql and found-8.0.sql from 8.0, percona-<version>.sql); schema-forge import from A; schema-forge write into a fresh server B; schema-forge import from B; A kept running until B is read; the two designs compared as equal says, and every object's DDL compared on A and B as equal says: equal, or each difference listed (counts only for a private schema). --option passes a server option a schema was written for to A and B alike (the old production schema needs --innodb-strict-mode=OFF on 8.0); --source reads a server already running in place of A (found with tools/local/containers.py), its password from a file of mode 600, never committed, its DDL not compared since the tool did not start it. It also lists, per table, every column that is NULL or its default in every row of design A and is not in unfilled, so a mapping that fills nothing shows; the PR carries that list. It prints the ImportReport of A and the write's time. --private FILE loads the owner's private schema instead (never committed; counts only, never names). --generated N writes into A a schema of N objects made by the tool (tables with columns, keys, foreign keys and indexes, views reading them, routines and triggers), the same every run, never committed; with it the tool fails when the import takes more than --import-limit seconds or the write more than --write-limit seconds.

tests.prove: a statement running past the endpoint's statement timeout is cancelled with SQLSTATE 57014; after a failed read on a pool of one connection the next read on it succeeds; every connection's configuration has the keepalives and the timeout (crates/core/tests/cortex.rs and crates/store unit tests)
the registry finds each engine by its id once; a Source's Debug never shows its password (crates/engine unit tests)
an object's key has a typed scope and kind; a reference to an object the catalog does not have is an error naming it (unit tests on a catalog built in the test)
an import's ImportReport.statements is at most the number of destination tables plus two, however many objects (integration test)
a failed import leaves its turn rejected and the design free for the next turn (integration test)
views in a cycle are an error naming them; a function without its return type is an error; triggers on one table, timing and event follow each other in action order (unit tests)
every MySQL type of the samples maps to an Arrow type with its fidelity (unit test)
the read's session settings are set to run after every reset of a connection and none only once (unit test on the pool's options: quirk driver-session-reset)
an account's hash is kept exactly as the server writes it, a quoted one, a binary one in hex and one holding a doubled quote (unit test on SHOW CREATE USER text from live servers)
partition and subpartition names written bare are read with their own options, and a subpartition count is not a listed subpartition (unit test on SHOW CREATE TABLE text from a live 8.0)
a check and an expression default are read as SHOW CREATE TABLE writes them, not as the catalog escapes them (unit test on text from a live 8.0)
only the first name of a dotted run is a view's own database when its definition is unqualified (unit test)
a bare password require current is kept as required (unit test on SHOW CREATE USER text)
a merge table's tables of another database are resolved in that database (unit test on a catalog built in the test)
listed subpartitions keep their own comments and counted subpartitions leave the comment on their partition (unit test on a catalog built in the test)
a table built unevenly is an error naming it and never padded with nulls (unit test)
a view comes after the functions it may call and a read-only database is closed after everything made in it (unit test)
a literal written under no backslash escapes keeps its backslashes single (unit test)
an account is written with its hash and a binary column's hex default as hex (unit test)
when the commit of a successful import fails the design the command made is removed (integration test: an engine whose import ends the turn itself makes the command's commit fail)
on each of the seven servers, the round trip's two designs are equal and every object's DDL is identical on server A and server B
a generated schema of 2,608 objects on MySQL 8.0 is imported in under 30 seconds and written in under 5 seconds on a CI runner
